aboutCagDesc1: CAG is India's constitutional auditor — an independent body that examines government spending and scheme implementation.
aboutCagDesc2: CAG reports reveal discrepancies, fund misuse, and implementation gaps.
aboutCriticalDesc: Major fund diversions, fraudulent claims, or complete scheme failure. Gap > 50% between claimed and actual.

aboutDataSourcesIntro: All data is sourced from publicly available government documents:
aboutDisclaimerText: Andhbhakt.org is an independent civic tool. We present publicly available data for transparency and accountability. This platform is not affiliated with any political party or government body.
aboutInfoNote: This platform is for informational purposes only. We encourage citizens to verify claims independently and engage in informed civic discourse.
aboutMajorDesc: Significant implementation delays, partial fund diversion, or misleading claims. Gap 25–50%.
aboutMinorDesc: Process issues, documentation gaps, or minor overstatements. Gap < 25%.

aboutWhatWeTrackP1: Andhbhakt.org is a civic transparency platform that compares official government claims (PIB press releases) against independent audit findings (CAG reports) for major schemes launched during the BJP era (2014–present).
aboutWhatWeTrackP2: We track the gap between political promises and ground reality — what the government said versus what auditors actually found.

incomeExplainer: Declared annual income of national parties from ECI filings (income tax returns submitted to Election Commission). Includes donations, membership fees, sale of publications, and bank interest.
incomeTrendFour: All figures are self-declared to ECI. Actual income (especially cash donations below ₹20K) is likely higher across all parties and years.
incomeTrendOne: INC led BJP in declared income every year from 2004-05 to 2012-13. BJP surpassed INC in 2013-14 — the year before Modi swept to power.
incomeTrendThree: INC's income collapsed after 2014 — from ₹682 cr (2014-15) to ₹198 cr (2017-18) — reflecting donor flight after electoral defeat.
incomeTrendTwo: Electoral Bonds (2018-19) caused BJP's declared income to jump from ₹1,027 cr to ₹2,410 cr — and again to ₹3,623 cr in the 2019 election year.
